script: Today I messed up by accidentally creating the perfect weight loss diet when I didn't need to lose weight. I just discovered the FU today, and it was like, boom, who knew my own kitchen could turn into a weight loss lab? I am a total food forgetter. I literally get so distracted that I don't even remember I am hungry until I am weak as a twig. Breakfast? Never. I'd just skip it and not eat until 3 pm, then I'd feel like I am running on empty. So I thought, "Okay, I am going to fix this." I started pumping protein shakes and porridge for breakfast, legume‑heavy lunches, and my usual chicken‑veg‑rice dinner. I was adding calories I never had before, so why not? What could go wrong? Fast‑forward to my medication review. The nurse pulls my weight—underweight, like dangerously so. I say, "Yeah, I am eating more." She goes, "Really?" My heart hits the floor. Panic mode. Hyperthyroidism? Coeliac? Cancer? We ran every test under the sun, and everything came back clean—at least for now. I still got to get a colonoscopy, though. (Yuk.) The real kicker? I was asked to track my food. Turns out I was eating more but getting fewer calories. All that fiber and protein kept me full but didn't feed me. Turns out, not all food is equal. People might call me an idiot, but my knowledge is "five a day" and fiber's my BFF because of the cholesterol and bowel cancer in my family. I thought I was being healthy. Now I am off to whip up a peanut butter banana coconut‑milk smoothie, drizzle olive oil on salmon and avocado, and still face that colonoscopy. It's a lesson: you can't just eat more and expect to gain. Sometimes the "healthier" choices are the ones that starve you.
